body ceb29fd9cb279e13 23 870
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// process.argv (WP7): a string[] built once by the @main wrapper from argc/argv.
// Index 0 is the program path (C's argv[0]), so the harness only prints the
// arguments from tests/cases/argv_echo.argv, which it passes to the binary.
function count() {
    return ((__nish.argv().length - 1) | 0);
}
function argument(i) {
    return __nish.idx(__nish.argv(), i);
}
export function main() {
    const args = __nish.argv();
    __nish.log(`${count()} argument(s)`);
    for (let i = 1; i < args.length; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        __nish.log(`${i}: ${argument(i)} (${__nish.strLen(__nish.idx(args, i))} bytes)`);
    }
    let sum = 0;
    for (const arg of args)
        sum = ((sum + __nish.parseInt(arg)) | 0);
    __nish.log(`sum of the numeric ones: ${sum}`);
    return args.length > 1 ? 0 : 1;
}

body 19e35313346baa22 26 978
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// WP15 §2: the negative test for the proof itself. The loop condition proves
// `i < xs.length` on the way in, but `drain` pops through the same array, so
// the fact has to die at the call — and the access after it keeps its check
// and panics. Run by the WP4 block of tests/run.js: exit 1 with "index out of
// range: 1 >= 1" on stderr, after three lines on stdout.
//
// `pop`'s result is discarded rather than returned, because `tsc` types
// `Array.prototype.pop` as `T | undefined` and this compiler types it as `T`
// (the one documented divergence in the ambient declarations); a case that
// returned it would be a second one.
const drain = (ys) => {
    __nish.pop(ys);
    return ys.length;
};
export const main = () => {
    const xs = [1, 2, 3];
    let i = 0;
    while (i < xs.length) {
        __nish.log(drain(xs));
        __nish.log(__nish.idx(xs, i));
        i = ((i + 1) | 0);
    }
    return 0;
};

body 2ad84e70cd75b160 22 847
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// `a[i] op= e` for the six bitwise operators. The array and the index are
// evaluated once, the bounds check is emitted once and the load and the store
// share one address, so a side-effecting index runs exactly one time: `slot()`
// prints once per statement, not twice, which is what the two lines of output
// before the values prove.
function slot() {
    __nish.log("slot");
    return 1;
}
export function main() {
    const a = [1, 255, 4];
    __nish.updIdx(a, slot(), __old => ((__old & 60) | 0));
    __nish.updIdx(a, slot(), __old => ((__old | 3) | 0));
    __nish.updIdx(a, 2, __old => ((__old << 33) | 0));
    __nish.updIdx(a, 2, __old => ((__old >>> 1) | 0));
    __nish.log(__nish.idx(a, 0));
    __nish.log(__nish.idx(a, 1));
    __nish.log(__nish.idx(a, 2));
    return 0;
}

import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
function trace(m) {
    let t = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < m.length; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        t = ((t + __nish.idx(__nish.idx(m, i), i)) | 0);
    }
    return t;
}
export function main() {

body 9b6b74f09288450b 32 896
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// `readonly T[]` is a type, not a parameter modifier, so it is legal wherever an
// array type is: a class field, a return type, a `const`'s annotation. The rule
// travels with it — a store through `h.items` is refused the same way a store
// through a parameter is — which is why the diagnostic says "declare it" and
// not "declare the parameter".
class Holder {
    items;
    constructor(items) {
        this.items = items;
    }
    total() {
        let sum = 0;
        for (const x of this.items) {
            sum = ((sum + x) | 0);
        }
        return sum;
    }
}
function labels() {
    const out = ["a", "b"];
    return out;
}
export function main() {
    const xs = [4, 5, 6];
    const h = new Holder(xs);
    __nish.log(h.total());
    __nish.log(labels().length);
    __nish.log(__nish.idx(xs, 2));
    return 0;
}

body 85cbbf35b8b2cf5b 27 1022
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// `readonly T[]` is the same array with every write refused, so a mutable array
// widens into it at the call and the callee still reads it every way there is:
// `length`, `a[i]`, `for...of`, `indexOf`, `join`. The golden is the point of
// the feature — it must be the IR the mutable spelling emits, instruction for
// instruction, because the flag is a promise to the checker and not a value.
function total(xs) {
    let sum = 0;
    for (const x of xs) {
        sum = ((sum + x) | 0);
    }
    return ((((((sum + xs.length) | 0) + __nish.idx(xs, 0)) | 0) + xs.indexOf(30)) | 0);
}
function label(parts) {
    return parts.join("-");
}
export function main() {
    const xs = [10, 20, 30];
    __nish.log(total(xs));
    __nish.log(label(["a", "b"]));
    // The array is still mutable here: widening happens at the parameter, and
    // nothing about `xs` changed by being passed to a `readonly` one.
    xs.push(40);
    __nish.log(total(xs));
    return 0;
}

function insertionSort(xs) {
    for (let i = 1; i < xs.length; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        const key = __nish.idx(xs, i);
        let j = ((i - 1) | 0);
        while (j >= 0 && __nish.idx(xs, j) > key) {
            __nish.setIdx(xs, ((j + 1) | 0), __nish.idx(xs, j));
            (((j = ((j - 1) | 0)) + 1) | 0);
        }
        __nish.setIdx(xs, ((j + 1) | 0), key);
    }
}
export function main() {
    const xs = [17, 3, 99, ((-4) | 0), 42, 8, 0, 23, 15, 61, 7, 88, ((-12) | 0), 5, 30, 2, 71, 19, 44, 1];
    insertionSort(xs);
    let line = "";
    for (const x of xs) {
        line = `${line}${x} `;
    }
    __nish.log(line);
    return 0;
}

body 3269c339349f2146 17 829
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// A stack array's slot is typed `[n x T]`, and `n` has to come from the length
// the source wrote. Under `--number-mode f64` the literal reaches the emitter
// as a register rather than as digits, because it has been converted on the way
// to an index: stage0 wrote `alloca [NaN x float]` -- IR `llvm-as` refuses, from
// a compile that exited 0 -- and stage1 wrote `alloca [0 x float]`, which
// assembles and then stores two floats past a zero-element slot (WP19 §A2).
function scale(k) {
    const xs = __nish.newArray(2, 0);
    __nish.setIdx(xs, 0, Math.fround(0.5));
    __nish.setIdx(xs, 1, Math.fround(1.25));
    return Math.fround(((Math.fround((__nish.idx(xs, 0) + __nish.idx(xs, 1)))) * k));
}
export function main() {
    __nish.log(scale(Math.fround(4.0)));
}

function fill(xs, n) {

import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// Typed-array aliases: Int32Array is i32[], Float64Array is f64[], BigInt64Array is i64[].
// They are the same StaticType as the element-typed array (one layout), so a
// Float64Array value is an ordinary f64[] argument and vice versa.
function sumI32(xs) {
    let total = 0;
    for (const x of xs) {
        total = ((total + x) | 0);
    }
    return total;
}
function sumF64(xs) {
    let total = 0;
    for (const x of xs) {
        total = (total + x);
    }
    return total;
}
function squares(n) {
    const out = __nish.newArray(n, 0);
    for (let i = 0; i < n; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        __nish.setIdx(out, i, Math.imul(i, i));
    }
    return out;
}
function scale(xs, k) {
    const out = __nish.newArray(xs.length, 0);
    for (let i = 0; i < xs.length; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        __nish.setIdx(out, i, (__nish.idx(xs, i) * k));
    }
    return out;
}
function widen(xs) {
    const out = __nish.newArray(xs.length, 0n);
    for (let i = 0; i < xs.length; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        __nish.setIdx(out, i, __nish.toI64(__nish.idx(xs, i)));
    }
    return out;
}
export function main() {
    const sq = squares(5);
    __nish.log(sumI32(sq));
    const ws = __nish.newArray(3, 0);
    __nish.setIdx(ws, 0, 0.5);
    __nish.setIdx(ws, 1, 1.5);
    __nish.setIdx(ws, 2, 2.5);
    const k = 2;
    __nish.log(sumF64(scale(ws, k)));
    const big = widen(sq);
    __nish.log(__nish.wrapI64((__nish.idx(big, 4) * 1000000000000n)));
    __nish.log(sq.length);
    return 0;
}

body 7dd23c3154228bc7 43 1803
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// A `u8[]` end to end: allocated, written, read back, and summed (WP30).
//
// The element type is what this case is for. A byte array is the payload shape
// a host hands a parser, and the whole reason `u8[]` can cross the interop
// boundary without marshalling is that `data` holds the bytes themselves —
// so the store, the load and the bounds check here are the same ones every
// other element width gets, at size 1.
//
// The sum widens with `toI32` at each element rather than accumulating in a
// `u8`: `u8` arithmetic wraps modulo 256, and 200 + 255 would be 199. That is
// the language's rule and not a quirk of arrays, but it is the mistake this
// case would otherwise invite, so it is spelled out.
function fill(bytes, v) {
    for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        __nish.setIdx(bytes, i, v);
    }
}
function sum(bytes) {
    let total = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        total = ((total + __nish.convert(__nish.idx(bytes, i), "u8", "i32")) | 0);
    }
    return total;
}
export function main() {
    const bytes = __nish.newArray(4, 0);
    fill(bytes, 200);
    __nish.log(`${sum(bytes)}`);
    // The top of the range, element by element, so a sign-extended load would
    // show up as a negative total rather than as 765.
    __nish.setIdx(bytes, 0, 255);
    __nish.setIdx(bytes, 1, 255);
    __nish.setIdx(bytes, 2, 255);
    __nish.setIdx(bytes, 3, 0);
    __nish.log(`${sum(bytes)}`);
    // Wrapping is the element's own arithmetic: 255 + 1 is 0 in a `u8`.
    const one = 1;
    __nish.setIdx(bytes, 3, ((__nish.idx(bytes, 0) + one) & 255));
    __nish.log(`${__nish.convert(__nish.idx(bytes, 3), "u8", "i32")}`);
    return 0;
}

body e53cfbee8f62b0b8 16 619
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// A shift count is masked to the *operand's* width, not to 31, so the narrow
// unsigned widths mask to 7 and 15. `a << 8` on a `u8` is `a << 0`, which is
// the JavaScript rule applied at a width JavaScript does not have; without the
// mask LLVM would make it poison.
export function shiftByWidth(a) {
    return ((a << (8 & 7)) & 255);
}
export function shiftU16(a, n) {
    return ((a << (n & 15)) & 65535);
}
export function main() {
    __nish.log(__nish.convert(shiftByWidth(37), "u8", "i32"));
    __nish.log(__nish.convert(shiftU16(3, 17), "u16", "i32"));
}

import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// `return g()` where `g` answers nothing. The call is the whole of the
// statement and the `ret` carries no operand, so the golden is read for a bare
// `ret void` with nothing after it: the spelling this used to emit,
// `ret void void`, is not IR at all and `llvm-as` refuses the module.
const emit = (n) => {
    __nish.log(`level ${n}`);
};
const walk = (n) => {
    if (n === 0)
        return;
    emit(n);
    return walk(((n - 1) | 0));
};
export const main = () => {
    walk(2);
    return 0;
};

// `p.f op= e` for the six bitwise operators: one GEP addresses the field, then
// a load, one instruction and a store, exactly as `p.f += e` does. The
// shift-count mask a local gets applies here too (`f.bits <<= 33` is a shift by
// one), and `>>=` still reads the field's signedness: zero-filling on the `u32`,
// sign-filling on the `i32`.
class Flags {
    bits = 255;
    wide = 4294967295;
    signed = ((-16) | 0);
}
export function main() {
    const f = new Flags();
    f.bits = ((f.bits & 60) | 0);
    f.bits = ((f.bits | 3) | 0);
    f.bits = ((f.bits ^ 5) | 0);
    f.bits = ((f.bits << 33) | 0);
    f.wide = ((f.wide >>> 28) >>> 0);
    f.signed = ((f.signed >> 2) | 0);
    __nish.log(f.bits);
    __nish.log(__nish.convert(f.wide, "u32", "i32"));
    __nish.log(f.signed);
    return 0;
}

class Counter {
    count;
    step;
    constructor(step) {
        this.count = 0;
        this.step = step;
    }
}
// Writes through `c`: no `readonly` on the parameter.
function bump(c) {
    c.count = ((c.count + c.step) | 0);
}
// Only reads through `c`, but passes it to `bump`, which writes: no `readonly` either.
function bumpTwice(c) {
    bump(c);
    bump(c);
    return c.count;
}
export function main() {

    c.step = 7;

class Version {
    major;
    minor;
    tag = "v";
    patch;
    constructor(major, minor) {
        this.major = major;
        this.minor = minor;
        this.patch = 0;
    }
    bump() {
        this.patch = ((this.patch + 1) | 0);
        return this.patch;
    }
    render() {
        return `${this.tag}${this.major}.${this.minor}.${this.patch}`;
    }
}
export function main() {
    const v = new Version(1, 4);
    v.bump();
    v.bump();
    v.patch = 9;
    __nish.log(v.render());
    __nish.log(((Math.imul(v.major, 100) + v.minor) | 0));
    return 0;
}

body edac4a8722523949 40 956
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
class Account {
    balance;
    fee;
    constructor(balance, fee) {
        this.balance = balance;
        this.fee = fee;
    }
    charge() {
        this.balance = ((this.balance - this.fee) | 0);
    }
    withdraw(amount) {
        if (amount > this.balance) {
            return false;
        }
        this.balance = ((this.balance - amount) | 0);
        this.charge();
        return true;
    }
    // Method recursion: drain in fixed steps until nothing is left.
    drain(step) {
        if (!this.withdraw(step)) {
            return this.balance;
        }
        return this.drain(step);
    }
    same(other) {
        return this === other;
    }
}
export function main() {
    const a = new Account(100, 1);
    __nish.log(a.withdraw(30));
    __nish.log(a.balance);
    __nish.log(a.drain(20));
    __nish.log(a.same(a));
    __nish.log(a.same(new Account(1, 1)));
    return 0;
}

body 160d6d9b4ee7ffe7 38 899
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
class Vec3 {
    x;
    y;
    z;
    constructor(x, y, z) {
        this.x = x;
        this.y = y;
        this.z = z;
    }
    dot(o) {
        return (((this.x * o.x) + (this.y * o.y)) + (this.z * o.z));
    }
    scaled(k) {
        return new Vec3((this.x * k), (this.y * k), (this.z * k));
    }
    addInPlace(o) {
        this.x = (this.x + o.x);
        this.y = (this.y + o.y);
        this.z = (this.z + o.z);
    }
}
function centroid(count) {
    const acc = new Vec3(0, 0, 0);
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        acc.addInPlace(new Vec3(1, 2, 3).scaled(0.5));
    }
    return acc;
}
// `main(): void` because under --number-mode f64 the literal `0` is a double.
export function main() {
    const c = centroid(4);
    __nish.log(c.x);
    __nish.log(c.y);
    __nish.log(c.z);
    __nish.log(c.dot(new Vec3(1, 1, 1)));
}

body ec31814d751c08a1 24 954
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// `f64ToBits`/`bitsToF64` reinterpret the 64 bits rather than converting the
// value: `toI64(1.5)` is 1, `f64ToBits(1.5)` is the IEEE-754 pattern. A
// compiler emitting LLVM IR needs this, because LLVM only accepts decimal
// float literals that round-trip exactly. Both lower to one `bitcast`, so a
// function that only reinterprets bits stays `readnone`.
function bitsOf(x) {
    return __nish.f64ToBits(x);
}
function valueOf(b) {
    return __nish.bitsToF64(b);
}
export function main() {
    __nish.log(bitsOf(0.0));
    __nish.log(bitsOf(1.0));
    __nish.log(bitsOf((-2.0)));
    __nish.log(valueOf(bitsOf(3.141592653589793)));
    __nish.log(valueOf(bitsOf((-0.5))) === (-0.5));
    // The sign bit survives the round trip through an integer, which is the
    // property that makes -0.0 distinguishable from 0.0 here but not with `===`.
    __nish.log(bitsOf((-0.0)) < 0n);
    return 0;
}

body ce3e91ba3f388884 31 1349
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// WP19 G1: `-g` measures a function from where its *declaration* starts, and
// for the arrow form that is the `const`, not the arrow. stage0 read the
// position off the `ArrowFunction`, whose own start is its parameter list, so
// it put `add` at column 20 where stage1 put it at column 1 — three
// `!DILocation` columns that left `node tests/run.js --parity` red. No `-g`
// case could ask the question, because every one of them was written in the
// `function` spelling.
//
// `span` is the half that pins the *line* rather than the column: its arrow
// sits a line below its `const`, so a compiler measuring from the arrow names
// line 19 in the `DISubprogram`, in `scopeLine` and in both parameters'
// `DILocalVariable`s, where the declaration a reader sees begins on line 18.
// `scaled` carries the `llvm.dbg.declare` of a slot, and `main` the artificial
// wrapper, which takes the user `main`'s position too.
export const add = (a, b) => ((a + b) | 0);
const span = (lo, hi) => ((hi - lo) | 0);
const scaled = (n) => {
    let acc = 0;
    for (const v of [1, 2, 3]) {
        acc = ((acc + Math.imul(v, n)) | 0);
    }
    return acc;
};
export const main = () => {
    __nish.log(`${add(2, 3)}`);
    __nish.log(`${span(1, 9)}`);
    __nish.log(`${scaled(2)}`);
    return 0;
};

// WP19 G1: a `!DILocation` column counts **bytes**, which is what `clang -g`
// writes and what a debugger reads the column back against. stage0 counted the
// UTF-16 code units the `typescript` API hands it, so the two compilers
// disagreed about every position that follows a non-ASCII character on its own

// inside a warning string, which is where `--parity` found it.
//

// the closing backtick on its line is two columns further along in bytes than
// in code units — the golden pins the byte count.
export const main = () => {
    const n = ((__nish.strLen("—") + 8) | 0);
    __nish.log(`${n}`);
    return ((n - 11) | 0);
};

// and a plain object literal inherits from `Object.prototype` — so before
// `src/lookup.ts` these compiled to `error: function valueOf() { [native code] }`.

    return Math.imul(x, 2);

// WP15: `String(x)` prints the fewest digits that read back as the same double,
// and "fewest" is not the same as "correctly rounded to that many digits". For
// these values the correctly-rounded 16-digit string does not round-trip but a
// neighbouring 16-digit string does, so the old snprintf/strtod search gave up
// and printed all seventeen. Ryu finds the shortest one, which is what Node
// prints and what this pins.
export function main() {
    const a = 7.120236347223045e-307;
    const b = 7.291122019556398e-304;
    const c = 8.209073602596753e-289;
    const d = 5.641232424577593e-278;
    // Ordinary values, to keep the common path honest alongside the rare one.
    const e = 0.1;
    const f = 1e21;
    const g = 5e-324;
    __nish.log(`${a}`);
    __nish.log(`${b}`);
    __nish.log(`${c}`);
    __nish.log(`${d}`);
    __nish.log(`${e}`);
    __nish.log(`${f}`);
    __nish.log(`${g}`);
    return 0;
}

body 37c8539d289af342 30 1172
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// WP22 §5.1: a module-level `const` bound to an arrow *is* a function
// declaration, so it is in scope for the whole module and not only after its
// own line. Nothing pinned that, and everything depends on it: `self/` is 721
// mutually recursive declarations in the order somebody found readable, and a
// rewrite that had to topologically sort a compiler to keep it compiling would
// not be a spelling change at all (§8b). `main` calls `isEven` above its
// declaration, and `isEven` and `isOdd` call each other, which no ordering of
// the two can avoid.
export const main = () => {
    __nish.log(isEven(10) ? "even" : "odd");
    __nish.log(`${countdown(4)}`);
    return 0;
};
const isEven = (n) => {
    if (n === 0) {
        return true;
    }
    return isOdd(((n - 1) | 0));
};
const isOdd = (n) => {
    if (n === 0) {
        return false;
    }
    return isEven(((n - 1) | 0));
};
// A concise body reaching forward as well, because §4's branch is the one that
// checks the expression rather than a block of statements.
const countdown = (n) => (n <= 0 ? 0 : ((n + countdown(((n - 1) | 0))) | 0));

body 9f27a491d6286352 25 1290
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// `getenv` (WP19 R1): the one environment read the language has, and the one a
// self-hosted driver needs to honour `CC` before it spawns `scripts/build.sh`.
//
// The three answers this pins are the whole contract, and the middle one is
// why the result is `string | null` rather than a string that is empty when
// nothing is set: `NISH_TEST_EMPTY=` is a variable that *is* set, and a
// driver that treats it as "unset, use the default" would be wrong. The values
// come from `io_getenv.env`, because the language has no `setenv` and a golden
// that read the developer's own environment would not be a golden.
export function main() {
    const set = __nish.getenv("NISH_TEST_VALUE");
    __nish.log(`set: ${set === null ? "<null>" : set}`);
    const empty = __nish.getenv("NISH_TEST_EMPTY");
    __nish.log(`empty: ${empty === null ? "<null>" : `"${empty}"`}`);
    const unset = __nish.getenv("NISH_TEST_NOT_SET");
    __nish.log(`unset: ${unset === null ? "<null>" : unset}`);
    // The narrowing is an ordinary `T | null` one: inside the guard the value is
    // a `string` and carries string methods, with no cast anywhere.
    if (set !== null) {
        __nish.log(`length: ${__nish.strLen(set)}`);
    }
    return 0;
}

body e25cf7d3e7e71c58 38 1450
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// `process.platform` and `process.arch` (WP14 §7a): what machine the compiled
// *program* runs on, which is the only question `--target host` is asking.
//
// A golden that printed the two strings would be a golden on one machine and a
// failure on the next, so what is pinned here is what does not vary: both are
// non-empty, both answer the same string every time they are read, and the
// pair maps to a triple this compiler supports — `hostTriple` below is the
// mapping `src/codegen/target.ts` and `self/target.ts` both make, spelled once
// more so the case proves the strings are the ones that mapping expects.
function hostTriple(platform, arch) {
    let cpu = "";
    if (arch === "x64") {
        cpu = "x86_64";
    }
    else if (arch === "arm64") {
        cpu = "aarch64";
    }
    if (__nish.strLen(cpu) === 0) {
        return "";
    }
    if (platform === "linux") {
        return `${cpu}-unknown-linux-gnu`;
    }
    if (platform === "darwin") {
        return `${cpu}-apple-darwin`;
    }
    return "";
}
export function main() {
    const platform = __nish.platform();
    const arch = __nish.arch();
    __nish.log(`platform: ${__nish.strLen(platform) > 0 && platform === __nish.platform()}`);
    __nish.log(`arch: ${__nish.strLen(arch) > 0 && arch === __nish.arch()}`);
    __nish.log(`triple: ${__nish.strLen(hostTriple(platform, arch)) > 0}`);
    return 0;
}

body 348771fb65f3a0db 22 955
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// `monotonicNanos`: the monotonic clock in nanoseconds as an i64. A golden
// cannot hold a timestamp, so this pins the two properties every run has —
// the clock does not go backwards, and it does advance.
//
// The bounded spin is what makes "it advances" a test rather than a hope: a
// `readnone` clock would let LLVM fold the two reads into one and the difference
// would be exactly zero forever, and a fixed amount of work between them would
// only be a bet on the resolution of whatever machine is running the suite.
export const main = () => {
    const first = __nish.monotonicNanos();
    let later = __nish.monotonicNanos();
    let spins = 0;
    while (later === first && spins < 10000000) {
        later = __nish.monotonicNanos();
        spins = ((spins + 1) | 0);
    }
    __nish.log(`monotonic: ${later >= first}`);
    __nish.log(`advances: ${later > first}`);
    return 0;
};

import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// `readdirSync`: a directory's entries, sorted by bytes and without `.` or `..`.
//
// The case builds the directory it lists, so the golden does not depend on the
// repository's layout, and creates every level itself because `mkdirSync` is not
// recursive. `b.txt` is written before `a.txt` on purpose: the order below is the
// listing's own, not the order the file system happened to store them in.
export const main = () => {
    __nish.mkdirSync("build");
    const dir = "build/io_readdir";
    __nish.mkdirSync(dir);
    __nish.mkdirSync(`${dir}/sub`);
    __nish.writeFileSync(`${dir}/b.txt`, "b");
    __nish.writeFileSync(`${dir}/a.txt`, "a");
    __nish.writeFileSync(`${dir}/.hidden`, "h");
    const entries = __nish.readdirSync(dir);
    if (entries === null) {
        __nish.log("unreadable");
        return 1;
    }
    // A dotfile is an entry, so the count is four and `.hidden` sorts first.
    __nish.log(`${entries.length}: ${entries.join(",")}`);
    // An empty directory is an empty array, which is not the `null` that
    // io_readdir_null.ts pins.
    const empty = __nish.readdirSync(`${dir}/sub`);
    if (empty === null) {
        __nish.log("sub unreadable");
        return 1;
    }
    __nish.log(`empty: ${empty.length}`);
    return 0;
};

// `realpathSync` (WP19 §5a item 4): the one path resolution the language has,
// and the one a compiler needs to find the package it was installed in when
// `argv[0]` reached it through a symbolic link — `ln -s /opt/nish/bin/nish
// /usr/local/bin/nish` is how a binary ordinarily reaches `$PATH`, and npm
// links every command the same way.
//
// The three answers here are the contract, and none of them is a path: an
// absolute answer is whatever machine this runs on, so what is pinned is the
// shape rather than the bytes. `tests/run.js` resolves an actual symlink in a
// directory it makes, which is the half a golden cannot state portably.
//
// The middle one is why the result is `string | null` rather than a string
// that is empty when nothing resolves: "does not resolve" is an answer the
// caller asked for, and every component but the last has to exist for POSIX
// `realpath` to answer at all.
export function main() {
    const missing = __nish.realpathSync("no-such-path-9f3c1a");
    __nish.log(`missing: ${missing === null ? "<null>" : "<resolved>"}`);
    const here = __nish.realpathSync(".");
    __nish.log(`dot: ${here === null ? "<null>" : __nish.startsWith(here, "/") ? "absolute" : "relative"}`);
    // The narrowing is an ordinary `T | null` one: inside the guard the value is
    // a `string` and carries string methods, with no cast anywhere.
    if (here !== null) {
        __nish.log(`nonempty: ${__nish.strLen(here) > 0}`);
    }
    return 0;
}

body 8c6acdcd86cdbe63 26 1036
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// `spawnSync` (WP14 D4): run argv[0] through PATH, wait, and answer the exit
// status — 128 + n for a signal (the shell's convention), -1 when the program
// could not be started at all and for an empty vector, which has no argv[0] to
// run. `sh -c` is the one program every POSIX host has.
//
// `run` is here for the attributes as much as for the reuse: the runtime keeps
// pointers into the vector it is handed, so `argv` must *not* come out
// `nocapture` or `readonly`, and neither function may be `willreturn`, because
// the child may never exit.
function run(argv) {
    return __nish.spawnSync(argv);
}
function shell(script) {
    return run(["sh", "-c", script]);
}
export function main() {
    __nish.log(`ok: ${shell("exit 0")}`);
    __nish.log(`status: ${shell("exit 7")}`);
    __nish.log(`signal: ${shell("kill -9 $$")}`);
    __nish.log(`missing: ${run(["nish-no-such-program"])}`);
    const empty = [];
    __nish.log(`empty: ${run(empty)}`);
    return 0;
}

// `spawnSyncTo`: `spawnSync` with each stream sent to a file, which is what
// comparing a child's output against a golden needs — `spawnSync` answers a
// status and the output is gone.
export const main = () => {
    __nish.mkdirSync("build");

    __nish.mkdirSync(dir);
    const out = `${dir}/out.txt`;
    const err = `${dir}/err.txt`;
    const status = __nish.spawnSyncTo(["sh", "-c", "echo to-stdout; echo to-stderr >&2; exit 3"], out, err);
    const captured = __nish.readFileSyncOrNull(out);
    const diagnostic = __nish.readFileSyncOrNull(err);
    if (captured === null || diagnostic === null) {
        __nish.log("nothing captured");
        return 1;
    }
    __nish.log(`${status}: ${__nish.substring(captured, 0, ((__nish.strLen(captured) - 1) | 0))} / ${__nish.substring(diagnostic, 0, ((__nish.strLen(diagnostic) - 1) | 0))}`);

    // run's bytes in front of its own.

        __nish.log("nothing captured twice");
        return 1;
    }
    __nish.log(`again: ${__nish.substring(again, 0, ((__nish.strLen(again) - 1) | 0))}`);
    return 0;
};

import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// Explicit arena control (WP6): Arena.mark / release / used / reset. A function
// that calls `Arena.release` or `Arena.reset` never gets an automatic scope.
class Blob {
    a;
    b;
    constructor(a) {
        this.a = a;
        this.b = Math.imul(a, 2);
    }
}
function fill(n) {
    const xs = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < n; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        xs.push(new Blob(i));
    }
    return xs;
}
export function main() {
    const base = __nish.arenaUsed();
    const m = __nish.arenaMark();
    const xs = fill(1000);
    __nish.log(__nish.idx(xs, 999).b);
    __nish.log(__nish.arenaUsed() > base);
    __nish.arenaRelease(m);
    __nish.log(__nish.arenaUsed() === base);
    const ys = fill(10);
    __nish.log(ys.length);
    __nish.arenaReset();
    __nish.log(__nish.arenaUsed());
    return 0;
}

import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// `getenv` bumps its result out of the arena, so a function that returns it must
// not get an automatic arena scope (WP6): the scope's `nish_arena_release` rewinds
// past the bytes the caller is about to read. This shipped broken — the value came
// back correct and was overwritten by the next allocation, which is silent
// corruption rather than a crash — so the case pins both halves: no scope in the
// IR golden, and the value still readable after 320 bytes of allocation on top.
//
// The template literal is what made the missing site visible: it gives the
// function an allocation that *does* flow locally, so there is a scope to get
// wrong. `mem_read_or_null_scope` is the same rule for `readFileSyncOrNull`.
const fromEnv = (name) => {
    const label = `read ${name}`;
    __nish.log(label);
    return __nish.getenv(name);
};

    const value = fromEnv("NISH_SCOPE_PROBE");
    if (value === null) {
        __nish.log("unset");
        return 1;
    }
    let filler = "";
    for (let i = 0; i < 40; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        filler = `${filler}ZZZZZZZZ`;
    }
    __nish.log(`filled ${__nish.strLen(filler)}`);
    __nish.log(`value: ${value}`);
    return 0;
};

body eaeaa8eef9703f63 74 1737
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// `T | null` (WP6): nullable fields, params, returns and locals; narrowing by
// `!== null` / `=== null` in `if`, early return, `while`, `&&` and `?:`.
class Node {
    value;
    next = null;
    constructor(value) {
        this.value = value;
    }
}
function sum(head) {
    let total = 0;
    let cur = head;
    while (cur !== null) {
        total = ((total + cur.value) | 0);
        cur = cur.next;
    }
    return total;
}
function find(head, want) {
    let cur = head;
    while (cur !== null && cur.value !== want) {
        cur = cur.next;
    }
    return cur;
}
function describe(n) {
    if (n === null) {
        return "none";
    }
    return `node ${n.value}`;
}
function valueOr(n, fallback) {
    return n !== null ? n.value : fallback;
}
function last(head) {
    let cur = head;
    let next = cur.next;
    while (next !== null) {
        cur = next;
        next = cur.next;
    }
    return cur;
}
export function main() {
    const a = new Node(1);
    const b = new Node(2);
    const c = new Node(3);
    a.next = b;
    b.next = c;
    __nish.log(sum(a));
    __nish.log(sum(null));
    __nish.log(describe(find(a, 2)));
    __nish.log(describe(find(a, 9)));
    __nish.log(valueOr(find(a, 3), ((-1) | 0)));
    __nish.log(valueOr(null, ((-1) | 0)));
    __nish.log(last(a).value);
    let s = null;
    __nish.log(s === null);
    s = "text";
    if (s !== null) {
        __nish.log(__nish.strLen(s));
    }
    const xs = __nish.newArray(2, null);
    __nish.setIdx(xs, 1, c);
    const x0 = __nish.idx(xs, 0);
    __nish.log(x0 === null);
    const x1 = __nish.idx(xs, 1);
    if (x1 !== null) {
        __nish.log(x1.value);
    }
    return 0;
}

import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// WP9: the returned temporary does not have to be concatenated for the reclaim
// to be sound. It is *kept*, not freed — `nish_arena_keep` relocates it and
// answers its new address — so what the caller does with it afterwards is its
// own business: pass it on, store it, return it. Only the bytes the callee
// bumped underneath it are released, and `allocEscapes` is what proves those
// are unreachable.
//
// Every call below is bracketed, and each one uses the *kept* pointer: passing
// the temporary to `shout` (`stack` is an argument, not a concatenation),
// handing it straight back out of `twice`, and storing it in a `const`.
function tag(i) {
    return `#${i}`;
}
function shout(s) {
    return (s + "!");
}
function twice(i) {
    return shout(tag(i));
}
export function main() {
    const held = tag(7);
    __nish.log(twice(1));
    __nish.log(held);
    return 0;
}

import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// WP9: a string-returning function cannot reclaim its own temporaries, because
// the one it returns has to outlive it. The *caller* can: the return value is
// the only thing a call hands back, so once `escape.ts` proves the callee lets
// nothing else out of its frame, everything it bumped underneath that string is
// garbage. `%arena.mark` before the call and `@nish_arena_keep` after it are
// the bracket; the kept string moves down to the mark.
function piece(i) {
    return `${i},`;
}
function join(n) {
    let s = "";
    for (let i = 0; i < n; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        s = (s + piece(i));
    }
    return s;
}
export function main() {
    __nish.log(join(4));
    return 0;
}

body dff19fb545149b27 46 1553
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// WP9 guard cases: three string-returning callees that must NOT be bracketed
// by the call-site reclaim, and one that must. The golden is read for absence,
// which is the whole point — a wrong reclaim is a use-after-free that no `.out`
// would catch, so the four calls in `main` are kept side by side.
//
//   fill    stores the string it built into an object its caller still holds,
//           so `allocEscapes` is true: those bytes are not garbage.
//   sweep   calls `Arena.reset()`, which moves the arena under any mark taken
//           around it (`usesArenaControl`).
//   label   returns a `Result<string, number>`, a pointer to a two-word object
//           whose payload was bumped *before* it. Only a plain `string` may be
//           kept, because only a string is one flat block with no interior
//           pointers; relocating the `Result` would free the payload it names.
//   plain   is the one that qualifies, and gets the mark/keep pair.
class Box {
    text;
    constructor(text) {
        this.text = text;
    }
}
function fill(b, i) {
    const s = `v${i}`;
    b.text = s;
    return s;
}
function sweep(i) {
    __nish.arenaReset();
    return `r${i}`;
}
function label(i) {
    return __nish.Ok(`L${i}`);
}
function plain(i) {
    return `p${i}`;
}
export function main() {
    const b = new Box("");
    __nish.log(fill(b, 1));
    __nish.log(b.text);
    __nish.log(sweep(2));
    __nish.log(label(3).unwrapOr("none"));
    __nish.log(plain(4));
    return 0;
}

body d181fd629c6c5c7e 35 1347
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// Automatic arena scope (WP6): `new Array<number>(n)` has a dynamic size, so it
// cannot go on the stack, but it never escapes `histogram`, so the function
// marks the arena on entry and releases it before returning. Called 100000
// times, `Arena.used()` does not grow (tests/run.js compares the two lines).
function histogram(n, seed) {
    const counts = __nish.newArray(n, 0);
    let x = seed;
    for (let i = 0; i < 1000; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        x = (((((Math.imul(x, 31) + 7) | 0)) % 1000003) | 0); // stays non-negative and far from i32 overflow
        __nish.updIdx(// stays non-negative and far from i32 overflow
        counts, ((x % n) | 0), __old => ((__old + 1) | 0));
    }
    let best = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < n; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        if (__nish.idx(counts, i) > __nish.idx(counts, best)) {
            best = i;
        }
    }
    return best;
}
export function main() {
    __nish.log(histogram(16, 1));
    const before = __nish.arenaUsed();
    let acc = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < 100000; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        acc = ((acc + histogram(((16 + (((i % 5) | 0))) | 0), i)) | 0);
    }
    const after = __nish.arenaUsed();
    __nish.log(before);
    __nish.log(acc);
    __nish.log(after);
    return 0;
}

// are released by the function's arena scope; a returned string disables it.
function label(i, name) {

}

        const line = (("hello, " + label(i, name)) + "!");

            __nish.log(line);
        }
    }
}

body e6250a564a4ae58e 21 927
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// WP6: a function with an automatic arena scope releases *before* a tail call
// whose arguments are all scalars, which leaves the call as the last thing the
// function does. Read the golden for the order: `@nish_arena_release` above the
// `call @sum`, not between it and the `ret`.
//
// The depth here is small because every case in this directory is also run
// under Node (WP13), and what that order buys is past V8's stack by
// construction: `tests/link/tail_call_depth` is the same shape a million levels
// deep, which is a segfault without the sink and a loop with it.
const sum = (n, acc) => {
    if (n === 0)
        return acc;
    const label = `item ${n}`; // the arena temporary the scope exists to release
    return sum(((n - 1) | 0), ((acc + __nish.strLen(label)) | 0));
};
export const main = () => {
    __nish.log(`${sum(1000, 0)}`);
    return 0;
};

body 42cdf49412116cb0 63 2579
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// WP6 guard cases: four recursions that look like the one in
// `mem_scope_tail_call` and must keep `@nish_arena_release` *after* the call,
// with no `tail` on it. The golden is read for that order, because sinking a
// release wrongly is a use-after-free or a wrong number, and only the first of
// those would crash.
//
//   walk   takes a `string`. That argument is arena memory above the mark, so
//          a release before the call hands the callee bytes the next bump
//          reuses. This is the shape that looks most like it should qualify.
//   watch  reads the bump position. Releasing first would not corrupt
//          anything; it would make `Arena.used()` answer a smaller number, and
//          `readsArenaState` is the fact that keeps the answer the same. The
//          value is deliberately unused: what disqualifies the call is the
//          read, not what the program does with it.
//   after  adds to the call's result, so the call is not in tail position at
//          all and there is nothing to sink it past.
//   Depth  is a method, and a method's receiver is an argument that the
//          argument list does not carry: `%this` is a pointer, so neither the
//          release nor the `tail` marker may be told that everything the
//          callee holds is a scalar. Comparing the parameter count with the
//          argument count is what refuses it — a signature with one more
//          parameter than there are arguments is one whose first argument was
//          never looked at.
const walk = (n, text) => {
    if (n === 0)
        return __nish.strLen(text);
    return walk(((n - 1) | 0), (text + `${n}`));
};
const watch = (n, acc) => {
    if (n === 0)
        return acc;
    const label = `item ${n}`;
    const bump = __nish.arenaUsed();
    return watch(((n - 1) | 0), ((acc + __nish.strLen(label)) | 0));
};
const after = (n) => {
    if (n === 0)
        return 0;
    const label = `item ${n}`;
    return ((after(((n - 1) | 0)) + __nish.strLen(label)) | 0);
};
class Depth {
    base;
    constructor(base) {
        this.base = base;
    }
    down(n, acc) {
        if (n === 0)
            return ((acc + this.base) | 0);
        const label = `item ${n}`;
        return this.down(((n - 1) | 0), ((acc + __nish.strLen(label)) | 0));
    }
}
export const main = () => {
    __nish.log(`${walk(3, "")}`);
    __nish.log(`${watch(3, 0)}`);
    __nish.log(`${after(3)}`);
    const depth = new Depth(100);
    __nish.log(`${depth.down(3, 0)}`);
    return 0;
};

// Array literals and `new Array<T>(<literal>)` that do not outlive the function
// live on the stack: `%arr.hdr = alloca %struct.nish_array` plus
// `%arr.data = alloca [n x T]`. A `push` moves the data into the arena but
// the header stays valid; a returned array stays in the arena.
function weights() {
    const ws = [3, 5, 7];
    let total = 0;
    for (const w of ws) {
        total = ((total + w) | 0);
    }
    return Math.imul(total, ws.length);
}
function zeroed() {
    const zs = __nish.newArray(4, 0);
    __nish.setIdx(zs, 2, 9);
    return ((__nish.idx(zs, 0) + __nish.idx(zs, 2)) | 0);
}
function grown() {
    const xs = [1, 2];
    xs.push(3);
    xs.push(4);
    xs.push(5);
    return ((__nish.idx(xs, 4) + xs.length) | 0);
}
function escaped() {
    return [10, 20];
}
export function main() {
    __nish.log(weights());
    __nish.log(zeroed());
    __nish.log(grown());
    __nish.log(__nish.idx(escaped(), 1));
    return 0;
}

class Registry {
    last = null;
}
// The constructor stores `this` into its argument: an Item outlives the
// function that created it, so `new Item(...)` must not become an alloca.
class Item {
    value;
    constructor(reg, value) {
        this.value = value;
        reg.last = this;
    }
}
function register(reg, value) {
    const item = new Item(reg, value);
    return item.value;
}
export function main() {
    const reg = new Registry();
    __nish.log(register(reg, 7));
    __nish.log(register(reg, 8));
    const last = reg.last;
    if (last !== null) {
        __nish.log(last.value);
    }
    return 0;
}

body 3e02fcbf19ad75ea 59 1540
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// Objects that may outlive their function stay in the arena (WP6): returned,
// stored into a field, pushed into an array, assigned to another local,
// handed to a callee that captures its parameter, or held by a reassigned `let`.
class Point {
    x;
    y;
    constructor(x, y) {
        this.x = x;
        this.y = y;
    }
}
class Box {
    item;
    constructor(item) {
        this.item = item;
    }
}
function keep(p) {
    return p;
}
function make() {
    return new Point(1, 2); // returned
}
function boxed() {
    return new Box(new Point(3, 4)); // the Point is stored by the constructor; the Box is returned
}
function stash(xs) {
    xs.push(new Point(5, 6)); // pushed
}
function field(b) {
    b.item = new Point(7, 8); // stored into a field
}
function captured() {
    const p = new Point(9, 10);
    const q = keep(p); // `keep` captures (returns) its parameter
    return q.x;
}
function reassigned(flag) {
    let p = new Point(11, 12);
    if (flag) {
        p = new Point(13, 14); // both objects are held by a reassigned `let`
    }
    return p.x;
}
function aliased() {
    const p = new Point(15, 16);
    let q = p; // `let q = p` is an assignment-style alias: conservative, arena
    return q.y;
}
export function main() {
    const xs = [];
    stash(xs);
    const b = boxed();
    field(b);
    __nish.log(((((((((((make().x + __nish.idx(xs, 0).y) | 0) + b.item.x) | 0) + captured()) | 0) + reassigned(true)) | 0) + aliased()) | 0));
    return 0;
}

// A per-iteration temporary in a hot loop (WP6): the alloca is hoisted to the
// entry block once and reused every iteration; the arena never grows.
class Vec {
    x;
    y;
    constructor(x, y) {
        this.x = x;
        this.y = y;
    }
    dot(o) {
        return ((Math.imul(this.x, o.x) + Math.imul(this.y, o.y)) | 0);
    }
}
function accumulate(n) {
    let total = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < n; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        const v = new Vec(i, 1);
        const w = new Vec(1, i);
        total = ((total + ((v.dot(w) % 7) | 0)) | 0);
    }
    return total;
}
export function main() {
    const before = __nish.arenaUsed();
    const total = accumulate(100000);
    const flat = __nish.arenaUsed() === before;
    __nish.log(total);
    __nish.log(flat);
    return 0;
}

class Point {
    x;
    y;
    constructor(x, y) {
        this.x = x;
        this.y = y;
    }
    manhattan() {
        return ((this.x + this.y) | 0);
    }
}
class Counter {
    count = 0;
    step = 3;
}
function sumX(p, q) {
    return ((p.x + q.x) | 0);
}
// An object literal that is only read: own memory, so the function is `readnone`.
function swapped(a, b) {
    const p = { first: b, second: a };
    return ((Math.imul(p.first, 10) + p.second) | 0);
}
// A class without a constructor: the initializers are stored inline, then written and read: `readnone` too.
function count(n) {
    const c = new Counter();
    c.count = n;
    c.count = ((c.count + c.step) | 0);
    return c.count;
}
// Constructed objects are allocas; the constructor still writes through `this`.
function nearest() {
    const p = new Point(3, 4);
    const q = new Point(10, 20);
    const alias = p;
    return ((((sumX(alias, q) + p.manhattan()) | 0) + new Point(1, 1).manhattan()) | 0);
}
export function main() {
    __nish.log(swapped(1, 2));
    __nish.log(count(4));
    __nish.log(nearest());
    return 0;
}

// WP20 T0: `--threads` (in the `.args` beside this file) gives every thread its
// own arena, and the whole of that in the IR is the storage class of
// `@nish_arena` — the inlined bump allocator GEPs the same declaration either
// way. The golden pins that one line; the `.out` says that nothing a program

//

body 4cdd83fce9af56f8 39 2030
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// WP15 §2/§8: a `substring` bound's clamp may only be folded on facts that
// hold where the *emitter* evaluates that bound. `emitSubstring` clamps
// argument 0 before argument 1 is evaluated, so nothing argument 1 does may
// reach back and prove argument 0. Judging both ends against the state the
// whole argument list left behind folded the clamp on a negative bound, read
// three bytes before the string body, and segfaulted once the offset was
// large enough -- with both compilers agreeing, so no oracle could see it.
function width() {
    return 6;
}
export const main = () => {
    const s = "hello world";
    // The reported shape: the assignment in argument 1 records `k <= s.length`,
    // and that fact must not reach the `k` the emitter has already read.
    let k = ((-3) | 0);
    const a = __nish.substring(s, k, (k = __nish.strLen(s)));
    __nish.log(`a [${a}] ${__nish.strLen(a)}`);
    // The same assignment one level down, in both arms of a conditional, where
    // the merge keeps it -- so reaching the call is not the same as being
    // written at the top of the argument.
    let m = ((-4) | 0);
    const pick = true;
    const b = __nish.substring(s, m, pick ? (m = __nish.strLen(s)) : (m = __nish.strLen(s)));
    __nish.log(`b [${b}] ${__nish.strLen(b)}`);
    // The other direction: a call in argument 1 takes nothing away from a bound
    // argument 0 already proved. A callee cannot reach a caller's local and a
    // string's length is fixed at construction, so `n` is still in range and its
    // clamp is still folded -- the golden is what says so.
    const n = __nish.strLen(s);
    const c = __nish.substring(s, n, width());
    __nish.log(`c [${c}] ${__nish.strLen(c)}`);
    // A literal `0` needs no facts at all, so it folds whatever argument 1 does.
    let j = ((-1) | 0);
    const d = __nish.substring(s, 0, (((j = __nish.strLen(s)) - 6) | 0));
    __nish.log(`d [${d}] ${__nish.strLen(d)} ${j}`);
    return 0;
};

body 59dc0873af893011 27 1476
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// WP15 §2/§8: `emitSubstring` loads the receiver's length before either bound
// runs, so a fact an argument states about the receiver *after* rebinding it
// is a fact about a different string -- and folding a bound on it reads past
// the string the call actually copies from. Interleaving the verdicts with the
// arguments is not enough on its own: this bound is argument 1, so it is
// judged after argument 0 either way, and what saves it is dropping the holder
// the moment an argument writes it.
export const main = () => {
    let s = "hi";
    const long = "hello world";
    let n = 0;
    // Argument 0 rebinds `s` and then bounds `n` by the *new*, longer string.
    // The length the emitter loaded is the old two-byte one, so the clamp on `n`
    // has to stay: without it the copy starts at the end of `"hi"` and runs
    // nine bytes past it.
    const a = __nish.substring(s, __nish.strLen((s = long)) > 0 ? (n = __nish.strLen(s)) : (n = __nish.strLen(s)), n);
    __nish.log(`a [${a}] ${__nish.strLen(a)}`);
    // A literal `0` is proven with no facts at all -- no string has a negative
    // length -- so it folds even after the receiver has been rebound. The golden
    // is what says the pair for it is gone and the pair for the other end stays.
    let u = "hi";
    const b = __nish.substring(u, 0, __nish.strLen((u = long)));
    __nish.log(`b [${b}] ${__nish.strLen(b)}`);
    return 0;
};

// `process.exit(code);` is a terminator: `finish` returns a number but ends
// with the exit call instead of a `return`, and the emitter closes the block
// with `unreachable` after the `noreturn` call to nish_exit. Both functions
// lose `willreturn`. The harness requires exit status 0, so `finish(0)`.
function finish(code) {
    __nish.log("exiting");
    __nish.exit(code);
}
export function main() {
    finish(0);
    __nish.log("not printed");
    return 1;
}

// `Result<T, E>` (WP16): the discriminant test is what unlocks the payload, so
// the golden pins one `load i1` plus a branch, and the two payload loads in the
// blocks the branch guards. Nothing reaches `value` without passing the test.
function half(n) {
    if (((n % 2) | 0) !== 0) {
        return __nish.Err("odd");
    }
    return __nish.Ok(((n / 2) | 0));
}

        __nish.log(good.error);
        return 1;

    __nish.log(good.value);
    const bad = half(7);
    if (bad.ok) {
        __nish.log(bad.value);
        return 1;
    }
    __nish.log(bad.error);
    return 0;
}

import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// WP17: `Result<i32, i32>` is small enough to travel in registers, so each of
// `half`'s two `return`s is one `insertvalue` rather than an arena bump. `half`
// is not exported, so what it answers is the private ABI's `{ i1, i32, i32 }`
// (WP15 §7b): the tag, the ok slot and the error slot, with the arm that is not
// live left `undef` — which is why neither `define` carries a `noundef` return
// attribute. An exported function packs the same value into one `i64` instead;
// `res_export` is the golden for that.
//
// The caller unpacks into its own entry-block object, which is what every WP16
// construct — `isErr()`, `.value`, `.error` — reads, so nothing below the ABI
// boundary changed. There is no `nish_alloc_struct` in this golden at all.
function half(n) {
    if (((n % 2) | 0) !== 0) {
        return __nish.Err(n);
    }
    return __nish.Ok(((n / 2) | 0));
}
export function main() {
    const good = half(8);
    if (good.isErr()) {
        __nish.log(good.error);
        return 1;
    }
    __nish.log(good.value);
    const bad = half(7);
    if (bad.ok) {
        __nish.log(bad.value);
        return 1;
    }
    __nish.log(bad.error);
    return 0;
}

import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// Every payload shape a by-value `Result` has to carry (WP17). `f32` is a
// `bitcast` in and out, not a conversion, so the bits the callee stored are
// the bits the caller reads; `boolean`, `u8` and `u16` are a `zext` in and a
// `trunc` out, and the two arms narrow separately because their LLVM types
// differ. The two constructions are also the two slots of the private ABI
// (WP15 §7b): the ok arm fills index 1 and the error arm index 2, each leaving
// the other `undef`.
function scale(x) {
    if (x < Math.fround(0)) {
        return __nish.Err(true);
    }
    return __nish.Ok(Math.fround((x * __nish.convert(Math.fround(2), "f32", "f32"))));
}
function narrow(n) {
    if (n > 255) {
        return __nish.Err(__nish.convert(1000, "i32", "u16"));
    }
    return __nish.Ok(__nish.convert(n, "i32", "u8"));
}
export function main() {
    __nish.log(scale(__nish.convert(Math.fround(1.5), "f32", "f32")).unwrapOr(__nish.convert(Math.fround((-Math.fround(1))), "f32", "f32")));
    __nish.log(scale(__nish.convert(Math.fround((-Math.fround(1))), "f32", "f32")).unwrapOr(__nish.convert(Math.fround((-Math.fround(1))), "f32", "f32")));
    const small = narrow(200);
    if (small.isOk()) {
        __nish.log(small.value);
    }
    const big = narrow(300);
    if (big.isErr()) {
        __nish.log(big.error);
    }
    return 0;
}

body a58f44d73b5bbaab 47 1492
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// The other three shapes a by-value `Result` has to cover. `Result<void, i32>`
// has no success payload, so `Ok()` is the bare constant
// `{ i1 true, i32 undef, i32 undef }` and needs no instruction at all.
// `orReturn()` in a by-value function builds the propagated error straight into
// the return registers instead of building an `Err` object. And `return r` on a
// variable loads all three slots and carries both arms: under the private ABI
// (WP15 §7b) there is no `select`, because each arm has a slot of its own and
// whoever ignores the dead one discards it.
function checkPort(port) {
    if (port <= 0) {
        return __nish.Err(port);
    }
    return __nish.Ok();
}
function firstHalf(n) {
    if (((n % 2) | 0) !== 0) {
        return __nish.Err(n);
    }
    return __nish.Ok(((n / 2) | 0));
}
function quarter(n) {
    try {
        const h = firstHalf(n).orReturn();
        return firstHalf(h);
    }
    catch (__propagated) {
        return __nish.caught(__propagated);
    }
}
function again(n) {
    const r = firstHalf(n);
    return r;
}
export function main() {
    const bad = checkPort(0);
    if (bad.isErr()) {
        __nish.log(bad.error);
    }
    checkPort(443).expect("443 is a port");
    __nish.log(quarter(8).unwrapOr(((-1) | 0)));
    __nish.log(quarter(6).unwrapOr(((-1) | 0)));
    __nish.log(again(10).unwrapOr(((-1) | 0)));
    __nish.log(again(11).unwrapOr(((-1) | 0)));
    return 0;
}

import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// process.argv (WP7): argv[0] is the program on both sides (the binary natively,
// the script under Node) and differs in text, so only its presence is checked;
// the rest comes from argv_words.argv. Every array operation applies to the
// read-only array (here: passing it on, `.length`, indexing, `for...of`).
function longest(words) {
    let best = "";
    let first = true;
    for (const w of words) {
        if (!first && __nish.strLen(w) > __nish.strLen(best))
            best = w;
        first = false;
    }
    return best;
}
export function main() {
    const args = __nish.argv();
    __nish.log(`${((args.length - 1) | 0)} words after the program name`);
    __nish.log(args.length > 0 && __nish.strLen(__nish.idx(args, 0)) > 0 ? "argv[0] is set" : "argv[0] is empty");
    let total = 0;
    for (let i = 1; i < args.length; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        __nish.log(`${i}: ${__nish.idx(args, i)} (${__nish.strLen(__nish.idx(args, i))} bytes)`);
        total = ((total + __nish.strLen(__nish.idx(args, i))) | 0);
    }
    __nish.log(`longest: ${longest(args)}`);
    __nish.log(`total bytes: ${total}`);
    return ((total % 256) | 0);
}

// 2D arrays: matrix multiplication, transpose, Pascal's triangle, jagged rows.
function multiply(a, b) {
    const out = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < a.length; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        const row = __nish.newArray(__nish.idx(b, 0).length, 0);
        for (let j = 0; j < __nish.idx(b, 0).length; (((j = ((j + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {

                s = ((s + Math.imul(__nish.idx(__nish.idx(a, i), k), __nish.idx(__nish.idx(b, k), j))) | 0);
            }
            __nish.setIdx(row, j, s);
        }

    }
    return out;
}

    __nish.log(pascal.length);
    __nish.log(__nish.idx(pascal, 7).length);
    const jagged = [[], [1], [1, 2], []];

// Index edges that are still in range: a[0], a[a.length - 1], computed indices, writes at the end.
function last(xs) {
    return __nish.idx(xs, ((xs.length - 1) | 0));
}
function rotate(xs) {
    const first = __nish.idx(xs, 0);
    for (let i = 0; ((i + 1) | 0) < xs.length; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        __nish.setIdx(xs, i, __nish.idx(xs, ((i + 1) | 0)));
    }
    __nish.setIdx(xs, ((xs.length - 1) | 0), first);
}
export function main() {
    const xs = [10, 20, 30, 40, 50];
    __nish.log(__nish.idx(xs, 0));
    __nish.log(last(xs));
    __nish.log(__nish.idx(xs, ((xs.length - 1) | 0)));
    __nish.log(__nish.idx(xs, ((xs.length / 2) | 0)));

import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// Bubble sort, in-place reverse, and a selection of the k smallest values.
function bubbleSort(xs) {
    let swaps = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < xs.length; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        for (let j = 0; ((j + 1) | 0) < ((xs.length - i) | 0); (((j = ((j + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
            if (__nish.idx(xs, j) > __nish.idx(xs, ((j + 1) | 0))) {
                const t = __nish.idx(xs, j);
                __nish.setIdx(xs, j, __nish.idx(xs, ((j + 1) | 0)));
                __nish.setIdx(xs, ((j + 1) | 0), t);
                (((swaps = ((swaps + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0);
            }
        }
    }
    return swaps;
}
function reverse(xs) {
    let lo = 0;
    let hi = ((xs.length - 1) | 0);
    while (lo < hi) {
        const t = __nish.idx(xs, lo);
        __nish.setIdx(xs, lo, __nish.idx(xs, hi));
        __nish.setIdx(xs, hi, t);
        (((lo = ((lo + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0);
        (((hi = ((hi - 1) | 0)) + 1) | 0);
    }
}
function show(xs) {
    let s = "[";
    for (let i = 0; i < xs.length; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        s = i === 0 ? `${s}${__nish.idx(xs, i)}` : `${s}, ${__nish.idx(xs, i)}`;
    }
    return (s + "]");
}
export function main() {
    const xs = [5, ((-3) | 0), 99, 0, 2147483647, ((((-2147483647) | 0) - 1) | 0), 42, 42, 7, ((-1) | 0)];
    __nish.log(show(xs));
    __nish.log(bubbleSort(xs));
    __nish.log(show(xs));
    reverse(xs);
    __nish.log(show(xs));
    const one = [1];
    reverse(one);
    __nish.log(show(one));
    const none = [];
    reverse(none);
    __nish.log(show(none));
    __nish.log(bubbleSort(none));
    const seq = [];
    let v = 17;
    for (let i = 0; i < 50; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        v = (((((Math.imul(v, 31) + 7) | 0)) % 1000) | 0);
        seq.push(v);
    }
    __nish.log(bubbleSort(seq));
    __nish.log(`${__nish.idx(seq, 0)} ${__nish.idx(seq, 1)} ${__nish.idx(seq, 2)} ... ${__nish.idx(seq, ((seq.length - 1) | 0))}`);
    reverse(seq);
    __nish.log(__nish.idx(seq, 0));
    return 0;
}

import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// `p.f op= e` and `a[i] op= e` for the six bitwise operators. JavaScript and
// Nish have to agree about three things at once here: the shift-count
// mask (`<<= 33` is a shift by one on both), the sign-filling of `>>` against
// the zero-filling of `>>>` on a negative value, and that the target
// expression is evaluated exactly once — which the counter `next()` bumps
// makes visible, because a target evaluated twice would print a different
// count on one side.
class Flags {
    bits;
    count;
    constructor() {
        this.bits = 0;
        this.count = 0;
    }
    next() {
        this.count = ((this.count + 1) | 0);
        return ((this.count - 1) | 0);
    }
}
export function main() {
    const f = new Flags();
    f.bits = ((-16) | 0);
    f.bits = ((f.bits | 3) | 0);
    __nish.log(f.bits);
    f.bits = ((f.bits & 255) | 0);
    __nish.log(f.bits);
    f.bits = ((f.bits ^ 170) | 0);
    __nish.log(f.bits);
    f.bits = ((f.bits << 33) | 0);
    __nish.log(f.bits);
    f.bits = ((f.bits >> 1) | 0);
    __nish.log(f.bits);
    f.bits = ((-256) | 0);
    f.bits = ((f.bits >>> 4) | 0);
    __nish.log(f.bits);
    // A variable count on an element target, across and past the width.
    for (let n = 0; n < 40; (((n = ((n + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        const b = [1, ((-16) | 0)];
        __nish.updIdx(b, 0, __old => ((__old << n) | 0));
        __nish.updIdx(b, 1, __old => ((__old >> n) | 0));
        __nish.log(`${__nish.idx(b, 0)} ${__nish.idx(b, 1)}`);
    }
    const a = [((-16) | 0), 255, 1];
    __nish.updIdx(a, f.next(), __old => ((__old >>> 2) | 0));
    __nish.updIdx(a, f.next(), __old => ((__old & 60) | 0));
    __nish.updIdx(a, f.next(), __old => ((__old << 35) | 0));
    __nish.log(__nish.idx(a, 0));
    __nish.log(__nish.idx(a, 1));
    __nish.log(__nish.idx(a, 2));
    __nish.log(f.count);
    return 0;
}

import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// FNV-1a: one `^` per byte and one wrapping multiply per round. This is the
// loop the bitwise operators were added for, and it is the reason the mask
// and the i32 wrap have to agree with JavaScript byte for byte.
function fnv1a(bytes) {
    let hash = ((-2128831035) | 0); // the 2166136261 offset basis, read as a signed i32
    for (const b of bytes) {
        hash = ((hash ^ b) | 0);
        hash = Math.imul(hash, 16777619);
    }
    return hash;
}
/** The bucket a hash lands in, which is what the `&` is really for. */
function bucket(bytes, size) {
    return ((fnv1a(bytes) & (((size - 1) | 0))) | 0);
}
export function main() {
    const hello = [104, 101, 108, 108, 111];
    const world = [119, 111, 114, 108, 100];
    const empty = [];
    __nish.log(fnv1a(empty));
    __nish.log(fnv1a(hello));
    __nish.log(fnv1a(world));
    __nish.log(bucket(hello, 1024));
    __nish.log(bucket(world, 1024));
    __nish.log(bucket(empty, 64));
    const bytes = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 256; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        bytes.push(i);
        __nish.log(`${fnv1a(bytes)} ${((fnv1a(bytes) >>> 24) | 0)} ${bucket(bytes, 4096)}`);
    }
    return 0;
}

// `<< >> >>>` on i32: sign-filling versus zero-filling, and counts at, above
// and below the 32-bit width. JavaScript masks the count to 5 bits and so do
// we, which is what keeps this program comparable at all.
function row(a, n) {

    __nish.log(`${a} >> ${n} = ${((a >> n) | 0)}`);
    __nish.log(`${a} >>> ${n} = ${((a >>> n) | 0)}`);
}

// `switch` against Node: the label grouping, the default edge, `break` and
// `continue` reaching past the switch to the enclosing loop, and an i64
// discriminant, whose labels are BigInt literals in JavaScript.
const KIND_SKIP = 3;
function classify(n) {
    switch (n) {
        case 0:
            return "zero";
        case 1:
        case 2:
            return "small";
        case ((-1) | 0):
            return "negative";
        default:
            return "other";
    }
}
function widen(w) {
    let out = 0n;
    switch (w) {
        case 1n:
            out = 11n;
            break;
        case 2n:
            out = 22n;
            break;
    }
    return out;
}
export function main() {
    for (let i = ((-2) | 0); i < 4; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        __nish.log(classify(i));
    }
    let total = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < 8; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        switch (((i % 4) | 0)) {
            case 0:
                total = ((total + 100) | 0);
                break;
            case KIND_SKIP:
                continue;
            default:
                total = ((total + 1) | 0);
        }
        total = ((total + 1000) | 0);
    }
    __nish.log(total);
    __nish.log(`${widen(1n)} ${widen(2n)} ${widen(9n)}`);
    return 0;
}

import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
class Savings {
    owner;
    balance;
    ops = 0;
    rate;
    constructor(owner, balance, rate) {
        this.owner = owner;
        this.balance = balance;
        this.rate = rate;
    }
    deposit(amount) {
        this.balance = ((this.balance + amount) | 0);
        this.ops = ((this.ops + 1) | 0);
        return this.balance;
    }
    accrue() {
        return this.deposit((((Math.imul(this.balance, this.rate)) / 100) | 0));
    }
    summary() {
        return `${this.owner}=${this.balance}/${this.ops}`;
    }
}
class Trust {
    owner = "trust";
    balance = 1000;
    ops = 0;
    beneficiaries;
    until = 12;
    constructor(beneficiaries) {
        this.beneficiaries = beneficiaries;
    }
    remaining(month) {
        return ((this.until - month) | 0);
    }
}
function total(accounts) {
    let sum = 0;
    for (const a of accounts) {
        sum = ((sum + a.balance) | 0);
    }
    return sum;
}
function richer(a, b) {
    return a.balance >= b.balance ? a : b;
}
// A write through the interface reaches the class's own bytes.
function charge(a, amount) {
    a.balance = ((a.balance - amount) | 0);
    a.ops = ((a.ops + 1) | 0);
    return a.balance;
}
export function main() {
    const s = new Savings("ann", 200, 10);
    __nish.log(s.deposit(50));
    __nish.log(s.accrue());
    __nish.log(s.summary());
    const t = new Trust(3);
    __nish.log(((t.remaining(1) + t.beneficiaries) | 0));
    const all = [s, t];
    all.push(new Savings("cat", 1, 1));
    __nish.setIdx(all, 1, new Savings("dan", 5, 1));
    __nish.log(total(all));
    __nish.log(richer(s, t).owner);
    __nish.log(charge(s, 25));
    __nish.log(s.balance);
    let best = s;
    best = t;
    __nish.log(best.owner);
    __nish.log(s.summary());
    return 0;
}

body 8b31c85903813759 42 1032
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// Collatz sequence lengths and peaks for 1..30 (do-while, while, nested loops).
function steps(n) {
    let x = n;
    let count = 0;
    while (x !== 1) {
        if (((x % 2) | 0) === 0) {
            x = ((x / 2) | 0);
        }
        else {
            x = ((Math.imul(3, x) + 1) | 0);
        }
        (((count = ((count + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0);
    }
    return count;
}
function peak(n) {
    let x = n;
    let best = n;
    do {
        if (x > best) {
            best = x;
        }
        x = ((x % 2) | 0) === 0 ? ((x / 2) | 0) : ((Math.imul(3, x) + 1) | 0);
    } while (x !== 1);
    return best;
}
export function main() {
    let longest = 0;
    let arg = 0;
    for (let n = 1; n <= 30; (((n = ((n + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        const s = steps(n);
        __nish.log(`${n}: ${s} steps, peak ${peak(n)}`);
        if (s > longest) {
            longest = s;
            arg = n;
        }
    }
    __nish.log(`longest: ${arg} (${longest})`);
    return 0;
}

import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// Digit sums, reversal, and palindromes with while loops, / and %.
function digitSum(n) {
    let s = 0;
    let r = n;
    while (r !== 0) {
        s = ((s + ((r % 10) | 0)) | 0);
        r = ((r / 10) | 0);
    }
    return s;
}
function reverse(n) {
    let r = 0;
    let x = n;
    while (x !== 0) {
        r = ((Math.imul(r, 10) + (((x % 10) | 0))) | 0);
        x = ((x / 10) | 0);
    }
    return r;
}
function isPalindrome(n) {
    return n === reverse(n);
}
export function main() {
    __nish.log(digitSum(12345));
    __nish.log(digitSum(((-987) | 0)));
    __nish.log(digitSum(2147483647));
    __nish.log(reverse(12345));
    __nish.log(reverse(((-120) | 0)));
    __nish.log(reverse(1000000001));
    __nish.log(reverse(2147483647));
    let count = 0;
    for (let i = 1; i < 2000; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        if (isPalindrome(i)) {
            (((count = ((count + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0);
        }
    }
    __nish.log(count);
    __nish.log(isPalindrome(12321));
    __nish.log(isPalindrome(12322));
    return 0;
}

import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// f32 against Node, which has only doubles. Every value here is chosen to be
// NOT exactly representable in a float, so a missing `Math.fround` in the
// rewrite shows up immediately: 0.1 prints 0.1 as an f64 and
// 0.10000000149011612 as an f32.
function scale(x, k) {
    return Math.fround((x * k));
}
export function main() {
    const tenth = Math.fround(0.1);
    const third = Math.fround(0.3333333333333333);
    const e = Math.fround(2.718281828459045);
    __nish.log(`${tenth} ${third} ${e}`);
    __nish.log(`${Math.fround((tenth + tenth))} ${Math.fround((tenth * tenth))} ${Math.fround((tenth - third))} ${Math.fround((third / tenth))}`);
    __nish.log(`${scale(tenth, Math.fround(3.0))} ${scale(third, third)}`);
    __nish.log(`${Math.fround((-tenth))} ${Math.fround((tenth % third))}`);
    // The same arithmetic in f64, for contrast: the digits differ.
    const dTenth = 0.1;
    __nish.log(`${dTenth} ${(dTenth + dTenth)} ${(dTenth * dTenth)}`);
    // Accumulating in f32 diverges from f64 after a few steps.
    let acc = Math.fround(0.0);
    for (let i = 0; i < 20; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        acc = Math.fround((acc + tenth));
    }
    __nish.log(`${acc}`);
    let counter = Math.fround(0.5);
    counter = Math.fround((counter + tenth));
    counter = Math.fround((counter * third));
    __nish.log(`${counter}`);
    // Conversions in both directions, including the saturating ones.
    __nish.log(`${__nish.convert(tenth, "f32", "f64")} ${__nish.convert(dTenth, "f64", "f32")} ${__nish.convert(third, "f32", "f32")}`);
    __nish.log(`${__nish.convert(tenth, "f32", "i32")} ${__nish.convert(e, "f32", "i32")} ${__nish.convert(tenth, "f32", "u32")}`);
    const negative = Math.fround((-Math.fround(2.75)));
    __nish.log(`${__nish.convert(negative, "f32", "i32")} ${__nish.convert(negative, "f32", "u32")}`);
    const huge = Math.fround(1e30);
    __nish.log(`${Math.fround((huge * huge))} ${__nish.convert(huge, "f32", "i32")} ${__nish.convert(huge, "f32", "u32")}`);
    __nish.log(`${__nish.convert(Math.fround(7), "f32", "f32")} ${__nish.convert(Math.fround(16777217), "f32", "f32")}`); // 2^24 + 1 has no float
    // Comparisons and Math on floats.
    __nish.log(`${tenth < third} ${tenth > third} ${tenth === tenth}`);
    __nish.log(`${Math.abs(negative)} ${Math.min(tenth, third)} ${Math.max(tenth, third)}`);
    // Float32Array is f32[]: stores round on the way in.
    const xs = __nish.newArray(3, 0);
    __nish.setIdx(xs, 0, Math.fround(0.1));
    __nish.setIdx(xs, 1, Math.fround((__nish.idx(xs, 0) * Math.fround(3.0))));
    __nish.updIdx(xs, 2, __old => Math.fround((__old + tenth)));
    __nish.log(`${__nish.idx(xs, 0)} ${__nish.idx(xs, 1)} ${__nish.idx(xs, 2)} ${xs.length}`);
    return 0;
}

export function main() {
    const limit = 50;
    const composite = __nish.newArray(((limit + 1) | 0), false);
    for (let i = 2; i <= limit; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        if (__nish.idx(composite, i)) {
            continue;
        }
        for (let j = Math.imul(i, i); j <= limit; j = ((j + i) | 0)) {
            __nish.setIdx(composite, j, true);
        }
    }
    let primes = "";
    for (let i = 2; i <= limit; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        if (!__nish.idx(composite, i)) {
            primes = `${primes}${i} `;
        }
    }
    __nish.log(primes);
    for (let i = 1; i <= 5; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        let row = "";
        for (let j = 1; j <= 5; (((j = ((j + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
            if (j > i) {
                break;
            }
            row = `${row}${Math.imul(i, j)} `;
        }
        __nish.log(row);
    }

        for (let b = a; b < 30; (((b = ((b + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {

                found = ((Math.imul(a, 100) + b) | 0);
                break;

                break;
            }
        }
    }
    __nish.log(`${found} after ${checks} checks`);
    let n = 0;
    do {
        let m = 0;

            (((m = ((m + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0);
            if (((m % 2) | 0) === 0) {
                continue;

// parseInt / parseFloat / Number over the command line (WP7): the numeric
// arguments are summed three ways; the odd ones out exercise the no-digits
// (0), trailing-garbage (parseFloat keeps the prefix, Number gives NaN) and
// saturation (parseInt clamps into i32) cases.
export function main() {
    const args = __nish.argv();
    let ints = 0;
    let floats = 0;
    let numbers = 0;
    for (let i = 1; i < args.length; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        const p = __nish.parseInt(__nish.idx(args, i));
        const f = __nish.parseFloat(__nish.idx(args, i));
        const n = __nish.number(__nish.idx(args, i));
        __nish.log(`${__nish.idx(args, i)}: parseInt ${p}, parseFloat ${f}, Number ${n}`);
        ints = ((ints + p) | 0);
        floats = (floats + f);
        numbers = (numbers + n);
    }
    __nish.log(`ints ${ints}`);
    __nish.log(`floats ${floats}`);
    __nish.log(`numbers ${numbers}`);
    __nish.log(`Number(ints) + Number(true) = ${(__nish.number(ints) + __nish.number(true))}`);
    return ints;
}

body 4c933248ef534cef 64 1832
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// Recursion: fib, ackermann, factorial (wrapping), gcd, mutual recursion, power by squaring.
function fib(n) {
    return n < 2 ? n : ((fib(((n - 1) | 0)) + fib(((n - 2) | 0))) | 0);
}
function ackermann(m, n) {
    if (m === 0) {
        return ((n + 1) | 0);
    }
    if (n === 0) {
        return ackermann(((m - 1) | 0), 1);
    }
    return ackermann(((m - 1) | 0), ackermann(m, ((n - 1) | 0)));
}
function factorial(n) {
    return n <= 1 ? 1 : Math.imul(n, factorial(((n - 1) | 0)));
}
function gcd(a, b) {
    return b === 0 ? a : gcd(b, ((a % b) | 0));
}
function isEven(n) {
    return n === 0 ? true : isOdd(((n - 1) | 0));
}
function isOdd(n) {
    return n === 0 ? false : isEven(((n - 1) | 0));
}
function power(base, exp) {
    if (exp === 0) {
        return 1;
    }
    const half = power(base, ((exp / 2) | 0));
    return ((exp % 2) | 0) === 0 ? Math.imul(half, half) : Math.imul(Math.imul(half, half), base);
}
function sumTo(n) {
    if (n === 0) {
        return 0;
    }
    return ((n + sumTo(((n - 1) | 0))) | 0);
}
export function main() {
    for (let i = 0; i <= 20; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {

// WP15 §4's `slice` against Node: the shim cuts the UTF-8 bytes, so a

// rather than clamping, and there is nothing to compare a panic against.

    __nish.log(`${__nish.convert(w, "u32", "u8")}`);
    __nish.log(`${__nish.convert(w, "u32", "u16")}`);
    __nish.log(`${__nish.convert(w, "u32", "u64")}`);
    __nish.log(`${__nish.convert(w, "u32", "f64")}`);
    const b = 200;
    __nish.log(`${__nish.convert(b, "u8", "u16")} ${__nish.convert(b, "u8", "u32")} ${__nish.convert(b, "u8", "u64")} ${__nish.convert(b, "u8", "i32")}`);
    const h = 60000;
    __nish.log(`${__nish.convert(h, "u16", "u8")} ${__nish.convert(h, "u16", "u32")} ${__nish.convert(h, "u16", "i32")}`);
    const neg = ((-1) | 0);
    __nish.log(`${__nish.convert(neg, "i32", "u8")} ${__nish.convert(neg, "i32", "u16")} ${__nish.convert(neg, "i32", "u32")} ${__nish.convert(neg, "i32", "u64")}`);
    const q = __nish.wrapU64((__nish.convert(0, "i32", "u64") - __nish.convert(1, "i32", "u64")));
    __nish.log(`${__nish.convert(q, "u64", "u32")} ${__nish.convert(q, "u64", "u16")} ${__nish.convert(q, "u64", "u8")} ${__nish.convert(q, "u64", "i64")}`);
    // f64 -> unsigned saturates at 0 and at the width's maximum.
    const over = 300.7;
    const under = (-5.5);
    const huge = 1000000000000.0;
    const inRange = 200.9;
    const wide = 3000000000.5;
    __nish.log(`${__nish.convert(over, "f64", "u8")} ${__nish.convert(under, "f64", "u8")} ${__nish.convert(huge, "f64", "u32")} ${__nish.convert((-huge), "f64", "u32")}`);
    __nish.log(`${__nish.convert(inRange, "f64", "u8")} ${__nish.convert(wide, "f64", "u32")}`);
    // Shifts. `>>` and `>>>` are the same on an unsigned type.
    __nish.log(`${((w >>> 1) >>> 0)} ${((w >>> 1) >>> 0)}`);
    __nish.log(`${((w >>> 31) >>> 0)} ${((w >>> 31) >>> 0)}`);
    __nish.log(`${((b >>> (3 & 7)) & 255)} ${((h >>> (5 & 15)) & 65535)}`);
    // The count is masked to the operand's own width, so these are shifts by
    // 1 and 2, not by 9 and 18. JavaScript would mask both to 31, which is why
    // the rewriter has to spell the narrow masks out.
    __nish.log(`${((b << (9 & 7)) & 255)} ${((b >>> (9 & 7)) & 255)}`);
    __nish.log(`${((h << (18 & 15)) & 65535)} ${((h >>> (18 & 15)) & 65535)}`);
    __nish.log(`${__nish.lshrU64(q, 32n)} ${__nish.lshrU64(q, 63n)}`);
    const s = ((-16) | 0);
    __nish.log(`${((s >> 2) | 0)}`); // ashr: stays negative
    __nish.log(`${((s >>> 2) | 0)}`); // lshr, read back as a signed i32
    const l = __nish.toI64(((-16) | 0));
    __nish.log(`${__nish.ashrI64(l, 2n)}`);
    __nish.log(`${__nish.lshrI64(l, 2n)}`);
    return 0;
}

body 6db3f12ba9a6705c 48 1648
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// Unsigned division, remainder and ordering. Every value here is above
// INT_MAX in its width, which is precisely where `udiv` and `icmp ult` differ
// from the signed instructions: as an i32, 4000000000 is negative.
function divU32(a, b) {
    return ((a / b) >>> 0);
}
function ltU32(a, b) {
    return a < b;
}
export function main() {
    const big = 4000000000;
    const small = 7;
    __nish.log(`${divU32(big, small)}`);
    __nish.log(`${((big % small) >>> 0)}`);
    __nish.log(`${divU32(big, big)}`);
    __nish.log(`${divU32(small, big)}`);
    __nish.log(`${((small % big) >>> 0)}`);
    __nish.log(`${ltU32(big, small)}`);
    __nish.log(`${ltU32(small, big)}`);
    __nish.log(`${big > 2147483647}`);
    __nish.log(`${big >= big}`);
    __nish.log(`${small <= big}`);
    const b = 200;
    const d = 3;
    __nish.log(`${((b / d) & 255)}`);
    __nish.log(`${((b % d) & 255)}`);
    __nish.log(`${b > 127}`);
    const h = 50000;
    __nish.log(`${((h / 7) & 65535)}`);
    __nish.log(`${((h % 7) & 65535)}`);
    __nish.log(`${h > 32767}`);
    const q = __nish.wrapU64((__nish.convert(0, "i32", "u64") - __nish.convert(1, "i32", "u64"))); // 2^64 - 1
    const three = 3n;
    __nish.log(`${__nish.wrapU64((q / three))}`);
    __nish.log(`${__nish.wrapU64((q % three))}`);
    __nish.log(`${q > three}`);
    // A loop whose counter passes INT_MAX: the unsigned compare keeps going.
    let n = 4294967290;
    let steps = 0;
    while (n > 4294967280) {
        n = ((n - 2) >>> 0);
        steps = ((steps + 1) >>> 0);
    }
    __nish.log(`${n} ${steps}`);
    return 0;
}

body 90ef4896e0a39675 47 1588
import * as __nish from "<root>/runtime/shim.mjs";
// Unsigned arithmetic at every width: wrapping `+ - *` at the top of each
// range, and values above INT_MAX that a signed type could not hold.
function mulU32(a, b) {
    return (Math.imul(a, b) >>> 0);
}
export function main() {
    const b0 = 255;
    __nish.log(`${((b0 + 1) & 255)}`);
    __nish.log(`${((b0 * 2) & 255)}`);
    __nish.log(`${((b0 - 255) & 255)}`);
    const b1 = 0;
    __nish.log(`${((b1 - 1) & 255)}`);
    __nish.log(`${((b1 - 200) & 255)}`);
    const h0 = 65535;
    __nish.log(`${((h0 + 1) & 65535)}`);
    __nish.log(`${((h0 * 3) & 65535)}`);
    const h1 = 0;
    __nish.log(`${((h1 - 1) & 65535)}`);
    const w0 = 4294967295;
    __nish.log(`${w0}`);
    __nish.log(`${((w0 + 1) >>> 0)}`);
    __nish.log(`${((w0 - 4294967295) >>> 0)}`);
    const w1 = 0;
    __nish.log(`${((w1 - 1) >>> 0)}`);
    __nish.log(`${mulU32(65536, 65536)}`);
    __nish.log(`${mulU32(3000000000, 3)}`);
    __nish.log(`${mulU32(123456789, 987654321)}`);
    const q0 = 0n;
    const one = 1n;
    __nish.log(`${__nish.wrapU64((q0 - one))}`);
    __nish.log(`${__nish.wrapU64((__nish.wrapU64((q0 - one)) - one))}`);
    const q1 = 4294967295n;
    __nish.log(`${__nish.wrapU64((q1 * q1))}`);
    let acc = 1;
    for (let i = 0; i < 40; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        acc = (((Math.imul(acc, 3) >>> 0) + 1) >>> 0);
    }
    __nish.log(`${acc}`);
    let byte = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < 1000; (((i = ((i + 1) | 0)) - 1) | 0)) {
        byte = ((byte + 7) & 255);
    }
    __nish.log(`${byte}`);
    return 0;
}
